canDo: Can say when, where and for how long, and arrange a simple schedule.
input: Listening: travel times, changes of place; reading: timetables/appointment notices.
output: Write an 80-word schedule; explain aloud your route and travel time from home to a destination.
checkpoint: ≥80% correct on prepositions of time and place; can tell apart the core uses of depuis and pendant.
challenge: Today’s challenge: write out your real schedule for tomorrow in French (at least 5 times of day), using à, en, depuis, pendant and a frequency word (souvent / tous les jours); then spend 1 minute explaining aloud your route from home to school or work and how long it takes.

questions.why: On Wednesdays the bassin sportif closes early at 19 h (« le mercredi, il ferme à 19 h »). 20 h is the time on other weekdays; handing the pool over to clubs explains why it closes early — it is not a condition for individual entry.
« n'ouvre que l'après-midi, sauf le samedi » — sauf introduces the only exception. 7 h–9 h is the slot of the bassin sportif, not the leisure pool.
The end of the text says clearly « et non par téléphone ». mardi/jeudi soir are class times, not a way of signing up.
libre depuis le 1er juillet → about two months by September. depuis marks the starting point; you have to work out the length yourself.
Ten minutes is the distance to the university; the third floor is the floor — other numbers in the same passage.
« je travaille tous les samedis pendant les vacances ». The Saturday-morning clean is a house rule, not her reason for saying no; 18–20 h is the Thursday slot.

« à trois cents mètres de la salle des fêtes » gets the direction of the distance the wrong way round: three hundred metres is measured from the square to the car park. The square itself is under construction.
« le marché du mercredi et du samedi » — two days.
Tuesday is not a market day, so « limité à deux heures le reste de la semaine » applies. Free unlimited parking is only on market days; 13 h 30 is when the stalls pack up.
pendant dix semaines is the length of the whole session. Fifteen days is how early you must register; two evenings is the weekly frequency.
Monday and Thursday are class times; fifteen days before refers to the registration deadline.

The end of the text says that the third unannounced absence ends your registration. liste d'attente is the consequence of registering too late; emailing the day before is what should have been done and wasn’t.
The reason is that the doctor is away all week. The carte Vitale is only a reminder at the end; the opening hours are extra information, not the reason for the call.
Two slots are offered: Thursday morning and late Friday afternoon. Saturday morning is only mentioned as opening hours, not as an option for rebooking.
avant vendredi midi. Tuesday at 11 was the original, cancelled appointment; 19 is when the practice closes.
The announcement first gives the delay, then the platform change. Saint-Brieuc is where people change trains, not the destination.
environ vingt minutes is the only length of time given; 14 h 20 was the scheduled departure.
19 heures is when the ticket office closes, not a requirement to wait.
sauf le dimanche is the key restriction; 20 août is the deadline for collecting the book, not for the opening period.
Note the difference between depuis (starting point) and pendant (length): 3 mars is when the library card became valid.
The message gives one clear solution: rappelez-nous.
The agent deliberately distinguishes première utilisation from achat; septembre is when the address started.
complément 1,80 € is the only solution mentioned.
This question tests depuis + a point in time directly; trente jours belongs to the pendant structure.

V04-31.exZh: Applications that arrive too late are put on a waiting list.

title: Time, place and arrangements
